tool.name: BWA-MEM3
tool.description: - map medium and long reads (> 100 bp) against reference genome
tool.command:
@pipefail@ @set_reference_fasta_filename@
## Begin BWA-MEM3 command line
bwa-mem3 mem #if str( $output_sort ) == "unsorted": -t 1 #else -t "\${GALAXY_SLOTS:-1}" #end if ## Verbosity is set to 1 (errors only) -v 1
#if str( $fastq_input.fastq_input_selector ) == "paired_iv": ## For interleaved fastq files set -p option -p ## check that insert statistics is used #if str( $fastq_input.iset_stats ): -I '${fastq_input.iset_stats}' #end if #end if
#if str( $analysis_type.analysis_type_selector ) == "full": ## Algorithmic options #if str( $analysis_type.algorithmic_options.algorithmic_options_selector ) == "set": -k '${analysis_type.algorithmic_options.k}' -w '${analysis_type.algorithmic_options.w}' -d '${analysis_type.algorithmic_options.d}' -r '${analysis_type.algorithmic_options.r}' -y '${analysis_type.algorithmic_options.y}' -c '${analysis_type.algorithmic_options.c}' -D '${analysis_type.algorithmic_options.D}' -W '${analysis_type.algorithmic_options.W}' -m '${analysis_type.algorithmic_options.m}' ${analysis_type.algorithmic_options.S} ${analysis_type.algorithmic_options.P} #end if
## Scoring options #if str( $analysis_type.scoring_options.scoring_options_selector ) == "set": -A '${analysis_type.scoring_options.A}' -B '${analysis_type.scoring_options.B}' -O '${analysis_type.scoring_options.O}' -E '${analysis_type.scoring_options.E}' -L '${analysis_type.scoring_options.L}' -U '${analysis_type.scoring_options.U}' #end if
## IO options #if str( $analysis_type.io_options.io_options_selector ) == "set": -T '${analysis_type.io_options.T}' -h '${analysis_type.io_options.h}' ${analysis_type.io_options.a} ${analysis_type.io_options.C} ${analysis_type.io_options.V} ${analysis_type.io_options.Y} ${analysis_type.io_options.M} ${analysis_type.io_options.five} ${analysis_type.io_options.q} #if str( $analysis_type.io_options.K ): -K '${analysis_type.io_options.K}' #end if #end if
## BWA-MEM3 performance options #if str( $analysis_type.performance_options.performance_options_selector ) == "set": ${analysis_type.performance_options.fast} ${analysis_type.performance_options.smem_dedup} ${analysis_type.performance_options.skip_contained_ext} ${analysis_type.performance_options.adaptive_band} #if str( $analysis_type.performance_options.max_extend_chains ): --max-extend-chains '${analysis_type.performance_options.max_extend_chains}' #end if #end if
#end if
## Handle read group options... @define_read_group_helpers@ #if str( $fastq_input.fastq_input_selector ) == "paired": #set $rg_auto_name = $read_group_name_default($fastq_input.fastq_input1, $fastq_input.fastq_input2) #else: #set $rg_auto_name = $read_group_name_default($fastq_input.fastq_input1) #end if @set_use_rg_var@ @set_read_group_vars@ #if $use_rg @set_rg_string@ -R '$rg_string' #end if
#if str( $fastq_input.fastq_input_selector ) == "paired": ## check that insert statistics is used #if str( $fastq_input.iset_stats ): -I '${fastq_input.iset_stats}' #end if
'${reference_fasta_filename}' '${fastq_input.fastq_input1}' '${fastq_input.fastq_input2}' #elif str( $fastq_input.fastq_input_selector ) == "paired_collection": ## check that insert statistics is used #if str( $fastq_input.iset_stats ): -I '${fastq_input.iset_stats}' #end if
'${reference_fasta_filename}' '${fastq_input.fastq_input1.forward}' '${fastq_input.fastq_input1.reverse}' #else: '${reference_fasta_filename}' '${fastq_input.fastq_input1}' #end if
#if str( $output_sort ) == "coordinate": | samtools sort -@\${GALAXY_SLOTS:-2} -T "\${TMPDIR:-.}" -O bam -o '$bam_output' #elif str( $output_sort ) == "name": | samtools sort -n -@\${GALAXY_SLOTS:-2} -T "\${TMPDIR:-.}" -O bam -o '$bam_output' #else | samtools view -@ \${GALAXY_SLOTS:-2} -bS - -o '$bam_output' #end if

param.name: fastq_input_selector
param.label: Single or Paired-end reads
param.help: Select between paired and single end data

param.name: fastq_input1
param.label: Select first set of reads

param.label: Select second set of reads

param.help: -I; This parameter is only used for paired reads. Only mean is required while sd, max, and min will be inferred. Examples: both "250" and "250,25" will work while "250,,10" will not. See below for details.

param.name: fastq_input1

param.label: Select a paired collection
param.help: See help section for an explanation of dataset collections

param.help: -I; This parameter is only used for paired reads. Only mean is required while sd, max, and min will be inferred. Examples: both "250" and "250,25" will work while "250,,10" will not. See below for details.

param.name: fastq_input1
param.label: Select fastq dataset

param.name: iset_stats
param.label: Enter mean, standard deviation, max, and min for insert lengths.
param.help: -I; This parameter is only used for paired reads. Only mean is required while sd, max, and min will be inferred. Examples: both "250" and "250,25" will work while "250,,10" will not. See below for details.

param.name: analysis_type_selector
param.label: Select analysis mode

param.name: algorithmic_options_selector
param.label: Set algorithmic options?

param.name: k
param.label: Minimum seed length

param.name: w
param.label: Band width for banded alignment

param.name: d
param.label: Off-diagonal X-dropoff

param.name: r
param.label: Look for internal seeds inside a seed longer than -k * THIS VALUE
param.help: -r; default=1.5; This is a key heuristic parameter for tuning the performance. Larger value yields fewer seeds, which leads to faster alignment speed but lower accuracy

param.name: y
param.label: Seed occurrence for the 3rd round seeding

param.name: c
param.label: Skip seeds with more than that many occurrences

param.name: D
param.label: Drop chains shorter than this fraction of the longest overlapping chain

param.name: W
param.label: Discard a chain if seeded bases shorter than THIS VALUE

param.name: m
param.label: Perform at most this many rounds of mate rescues for each read

param.name: S
param.label: Skip mate rescue

param.name: P
param.label: Skip pairing; mate rescue performed unless -S also in use

param.name: scoring_options_selector
param.label: Set scoring options?

param.name: A
param.label: Score for a sequence match
param.help: -A; scales options -T, -d, -B, -O, -E, -L, and -U unless overridden; default=1

param.name: B
param.label: Penalty for a mismatch

param.name: O
param.label: Gap open penalties for deletions and insertions

param.name: E
param.label: Gap extension penalties; a gap of size k cost '-O + -E*k'. If two numbers are specified, the first is the penalty of extending a deletion and the second for extending an insertion

param.name: L
param.label: Penalties for 5'-end and 3'-end clipping
param.help: -L; default=5,5; When performing Smith-Waterman extension, BWA-MEM keeps track of the best score reaching the end of query. If this score is larger than the best Smith-Waterman score minus the clipping penalty, clipping will not be applied. Note that in this case, the SAM AS tag reports the best Smith-Waterman score; clipping penalty is not deduced

param.name: U
param.label: Penalty for an unpaired read pair

param.name: io_options_selector
param.label: Set input/output options

param.name: five
param.label: For split alignment, take alignment with smallest coordinate as primary
Don't lower MAPQ for split alignment
param.help: By default the MAPQ score of a supplementary alignment will be lowered to the primary alignment score.

param.name: T
param.label: Minimum score to output

param.name: h
param.label: If there are less than THIS VALUE hits with score >80% of the max score, output them all in the XA tag

param.name: a
param.label: Output all alignments for single-ends or unpaired paired-ends
param.help: -a; These alignments will be flagged as secondary alignments

param.name: C
param.label: Append FASTA/FASTQ comment to BAM output

param.name: V
param.label: Output the reference FASTA header in the XR tag

param.name: Y
param.label: Use soft clipping for supplementary alignments
param.help: -Y; By default, BWA-MEM uses soft clipping for the primary alignment and hard clipping for supplementary alignments

param.name: M
param.label: Mark shorter split hits of a chimeric alignment in the FLAG field as 'secondary alignment' instead of 'supplementary alignment'

param.name: K
param.label: Process this number of input bases in each batch regardless of nThreads (for reproducibility)

param.name: performance_options_selector
param.label: Set BWA-MEM3 performance options?
param.help: Extra speed heuristics available in BWA-MEM3. Some change the output and are NOT byte-identical to the BWA-MEM/BWA-MEM2 default; see the help of each option.

param.label: Enable the --fast speed preset
param.help: Bundles several speed heuristics (-m 10 -y 0 --min-ext-len 30 --smem-dedup --skip-contained-ext --max-extend-chains 5 --adaptive-band). Opt-in; NOT byte-identical to the default (divergence confined to the low-confidence tail).

param.label: Deduplicate identical SMEMs before chaining
param.help: Fewer SA lookups, ~10% fewer. Opt-in; NOT byte-identical (changes XS/secondary on a small fraction of reads).

param.label: Skip banded-SW extension of contained seeds
param.help: Skips banded-SW extension of seeds contained (same diagonal) in a longer in-chain seed. Byte-identical on short/medium non-methylation reads; ~10% less alignment CPU.

param.label: Adaptive banded Smith-Waterman
param.help: Start tight and expand each pair to its chain-geometry band on long-extension reads (long-read speedup, no-op on short reads). Opt-in; NOT byte-identical.

param.label: Cap chains extended per read to the top-N by weight
param.help: 0 = off. ~23% less alignment CPU; high-confidence placement unaffected. Opt-in; NOT byte-identical.

param.name: output_sort
param.label: BAM sorting mode
param.option: Sort by read names (i.e., the QNAME field)

tool.help:
**What it does**
BWA-MEM3 is a short-read aligner derived from BWA-MEM2, with correctness fixes, performance improvements, methylation-aware alignment, and a multi-tier SIMD runtime. On non-methylation data at default settings it reproduces the alignments of BWA-MEM/BWA-MEM2, while running faster. The algorithm is robust to sequencing errors and applicable to a wide range of sequence lengths from 70 bp to a few megabases.
The Galaxy implementation takes fastq files as input and produces output in BAM format, which can be further processed using various BAM utilities existing in Galaxy (BAMTools, SAMTools, Picard).
-----
**Indices: Selecting reference genomes for BWA-MEM3**
The wrapper lets you select between precomputed (built-in) and user-defined indices for reference genomes using the **Will you select a reference genome from your history or use a built-in index?** flag. This flag has two options:
1. **Use a built-in genome index** - Galaxy provides a **Select reference genome index** dropdown, populated with genomes that were pre-indexed with the ``bwa-mem3 index`` utility and are ready to be mapped against. 2. **Use a reference from history and build index if necessary** - Galaxy provides a **Select reference genome sequence** dropdown, populated with FASTA files in your current history. Selecting one causes Galaxy to first transparently index it with ``bwa-mem3 index`` and then run mapping with ``bwa-mem3 mem``.
-----
**Galaxy-specific option**
The **Select analysis mode** menu offers two levels of control:
1. *Simple Illumina mode*: aligns single or paired-end data to the reference using default parameters. Equivalent to ``bwa-mem3 mem <reference index> <fastq dataset1> [fastq dataset2]``. 2. *Full list of options*: exposes the algorithmic, scoring, input/output and BWA-MEM3 performance options through the Galaxy interface.
-----
**BWA-MEM3 performance options**
BWA-MEM3 adds extra speed heuristics beyond BWA-MEM2. Some of them are byte-identical to the default output (e.g. ``--skip-contained-ext`` on short/medium non-methylation reads); others trade a small, low-confidence-tail change in output for additional speed (``--fast``, ``--smem-dedup``, ``--adaptive-band``, ``--max-extend-chains``). Each option's help states whether it is byte-identical. Leave them unset to reproduce BWA-MEM2 output.
-----
**Bam sorting mode**
The generated bam files can be sorted according to three criteria: coordinates, names and input order.
In coordinate sorted mode the reads are sorted by coordinates, i.e. the reads from the beginning of the first chromosome are first in the file.
When sorted by read name, the file is sorted by the QNAME field.
Finally, the *Not sorted (sorted as input)* option yields a BAM file in which the records are in the same order as the reads in the original input file. This option requires a single thread to perform the conversion from SAM to BAM format, so the runtime is extended.
